title: Production Plan: Nuvei Connector for commercetools Connect
summary: Plan for building a Nuvei commercetools Connect payment connector covering architecture, phases, endpoints, security, runtime constraints, testing, operations, and readiness.
notes: Manifest declares DOC and is authoritative. Content contains plan/spec-like requirements, endpoint contracts, security constraints, architecture decisions, and a 'Locked scope' section, but it is not an Accepted ADR and is therefore not locked by classifier policy.
locked_decisions: Document states implementation start scope is cards only.
Document states Complete Checkout and Payment Only are in scope.
Document states custom checkout enabler support is in scope.
Document states authorization-first with delayed capture is the default lifecycle.
Document states DMN webhook processing is in scope.
Document states stored payment methods and express payments are out of initial scope.
Document states Custom Types should not be used unless Phase 0 proves they are necessary.
requirements: Build a private Organization Connector for Nuvei that works with commercetools Complete Checkout and Payment Only.
Support custom checkout storefront usage through the same enabler and processor.
Support physical goods with checkout authorization and later capture through Checkout Payment Intents API.
Processor must expose config, status, payment-components, payment-intents, transactions, Nuvei payment creation, Nuvei payment confirmation, and Nuvei webhook routes.
Map Nuvei Auth or PreAuth to commercetools Authorization; Settle or Sale to Charge; Credit to Refund; Void to CancelAuthorization; Chargeback to Chargeback.
Map Nuvei ppp_status OK to Success, FAIL to Failure, and other states to Pending.
Use Nuvei openOrder, getPaymentStatus, settleTransaction, voidTransaction, and refundTransaction endpoints.
Enabler must be a thin wrapper around the Nuvei frontend widget with business logic in the processor.
Support duplicate DMNs idempotently and reject invalid checksum DMNs.

Validate local, preview deployment, and sandbox deployment flows, including authorization, failure, pending/async, capture, cancel authorization, refund, duplicate DMN, invalid checksum, and expired or invalid session scenarios.
Provide structured logging, status checks, deployment documentation, retry policy, timeout budgets, Chrome browser E2E, and CI quality gates for production hardening.
constraints: Initial scope excludes merchant fulfillment rules, order management outside Checkout, OMS/ERP/fraud/tax functionality, all payment methods on day one, subscriptions or recurring billing, and extra commercetools custom fields unless proven necessary.
Nuvei integration target is existing Simply Connect / REST v1 style flow.
DMN webhook configuration is manual in the Nuvei dashboard.
Connector is deployed through commercetools Connect, not self-hosted.
Use standard Connect payment architecture with enabler assets and processor service.
Do not use commercetools API Extensions for payment creation, a separate standalone DMN app, or direct browser calls to commercetools Payments API.
Nuvei is source of truth for payment execution state; commercetools is source of truth for cart amounts, order references, and payment records; DMNs reconcile final state.
Default to SHA-256 for checksum and signature operations; do not support MD5 unless Nuvei demonstrably requires it, and then only explicitly, feature-flagged, and documented as legacy.

Frontend and session routes use sessionHeaderAuthHook.authenticate(); server-managed operations use oauth2AuthHook.authenticate() plus authorizationHook.authorize(...); status and internal routes use jwtAuthHook.authenticate(); webhooks rely on raw payload verification.
Webhook verification must preserve raw request body, use timing-safe comparison, reject malformed checksums immediately, verify merchant identity, and treat duplicate DMNs as normal.
No PAN or raw card data may be stored or logged; secrets, tokens, and checksum material must be redacted; raw errors must not leak to clients.
MVP processor client scopes start with manage_payments, view_sessions, view_api_clients, manage_checkout_payment_intents, and introspect_oauth_tokens, adding more only when needed.
Use pnpm with root packageManager field and corepack; validate pnpm in preview deployments.
Processor must serve HTTP on port 8080; each app must have valid start and gcp-build/build scripts.
Use oxlint and oxfmt; keep dependencies stable with pinned lockfile; avoid unnecessary dependencies.
Keep packages separate and avoid internal shared packages until duplication is proven.
Use short outbound HTTP timeouts; retry explicitly only where safe; use idempotency-key protection for payment creation.
